Description of Requirement:
The Department of Veterans Affairs, Veterans Health Administration (VHA), Network Contracting Office 19 (NCO 19) is conducting a market survey and is seeking potential sources for a Bayesian Dosing Software, including single site standalone licensing. This Sources Sought Notice is issued for information and planning purposes only. This is not a solicitation or a request for proposal and shall not be construed as an obligation or commitment by the Government. An award will not be made on any offers submitted in response to this notice, and it shall not be implied that the Government is committed to providing any solicitation or award following this notice. The Government will not pay for any information received in response to this request, nor will the Government compensate a respondent for any costs incurred in developing the information provided. 

Requirement Item: Bayesian Dosing Software Single Site - Standalone Licensing 

STATEMENT OF WORK
Introduction and Overview

This statement of work is for a subscription to a Bayesian-guided medication dosing software from a contractor that can provide licensing rights. This subscription is to ensure clinicians have access to a reliable web-based therapeutic drug dosing and monitoring tool for complex clinical situations that require careful drug therapy evaluation and adjustment in a systematic and efficient manner. The software will include important pharmacokinetic parameters and empiric and patient-specific dosing recommendations; allow for graphical prediction and projection of theoretical doses at any drug dosing interval in order to optimize and achieve therapeutic drug levels; provide local storage of data and references for primary literature of clinicals models used; and lastly, be highly customizable, HIPAA and GDPR compliant, and meet VA information security requirements by only providing patient de-identification information on the web-based platform. Must be fully compliant with the IDSA/ASHP Vancomycin 2020 guidelines.

Background

Intravenous vancomycin remains an important first-line antibiotic used for treatment of serious methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) infections. Recent Consensus Guidelines (Rybak MJ et al, AM J HEALTH-SYST PHARM, March 2020) for vancomycin therapeutic monitoring now recommend vancomycin dose optimization preferably using a Bayesian-guided software to achieve individualized targeted concentrations that maximize clinical efficacy while minimizing renal toxicity. Veterans Affairs Healthcare Systems are complex in scope of services; thus, clinical providers require access to a validated, systematic, and intuitive clinical tool to dose and monitor drug therapy safely. 

Scope of Work

The contractor shall provide all resources necessary and have an established Business Associate Agreement with the Department of Veterans Affairs to meet requirements and accomplish the deliverables described in this statement of work (SOW), except as may otherwise be specified.
The contractor shall provide uninterrupted licensing and subscription services to a Bayesian-guided medication dosing software as stated herein for clinical staff within the VA Salt Lake City Health Care System.

Requirements

License rights toÂ aÂ web-based pharmacokinetics medication dosing softwareÂ programÂ from a contractor that can provide license rights equivalent to or exceeding the product listing offered by theÂ proprietor.Â 
Web-based program that can be found from any web browser with an internet connection. 
Capability to integrate into VISTA and CERNER electronic health record (EHR) so the tool can automatically retrieve all required data available in the hospital s health records and use to provide estimated dosing recommendations. 
Provide input data storage capability with database searchable by patient name, patient identification, drug name, or date.
UnlimitedÂ andÂ simultaneous userÂ accessÂ must be available onlineÂ 24Â hours a dayÂ 7Â days a weekÂ via webÂ from any government owned equipment (authenticated by IP address)Â as well asÂ remote accessÂ forÂ virtual employees.
Provide capable de-identify patient data base for VA populationÂ 
Software to include additionalÂ drugÂ specificÂ factorsÂ that may influence the patient s pharmacokineticÂ profile or dosing regimen such as amputation, obesity, pregnancy,Â critically ill, burn patient, hematology/oncology patient, spinal cord injury, cystic fibrosis,Â significant drug-drug interactions,Â andÂ drug-disease state interactions.Â Â 
Software to include the option to incorporateÂ patient specific dataÂ points age, gender, weight, height, renal function,Â dosage history,Â drugÂ serum concentrations,Â dialysis history, andÂ previous vancomycin history.Â Â 
Software to display population pharmacokinetic parameters details such as clearance, volume of distribution, half-life, etc.Â 
Drug monitoring to include serum level graphs with options to display populationÂ data, individual/patient specific data, therapeuticÂ range,Â toxicityÂ and serum levels.Â Â 
Include ability to specify therapeutic targets (AUC, trough, peak) and receive recommended dose and interval based on selected target.Â Â 
Ability to propose recommended dosing regimens with and without patient serum drug levels, with ability to incorporate non-steady state and irregular situations.
Program to provide warning to user if there is detection of a potentially toxic dose, serum level, or if outside recommended AUC range.Â Â 
ProgramÂ to have option for inter-site sharing of patient case dataÂ including drug dosing and monitoring informationÂ 
Access to all drug kinetics offered within the program and any new drug kinetics added in the future.
Software to include Veteran population kinetic model using data based on the VA's specific population; model should be updated quarterly at a minimum; includes Vancomycin, Aminoglycosides, Antibiotics, Anticonvulsants, Antiarrhythmic, Antifungal, Oncology, Transplants medications. 
Reports and data analytics to be made available to users quarterly for users to access, download and/or print. 
Ability to generate patient specific and population reports that are customizable by the user. 

Tasks and Associated Deliverables

The contractor shall provide a detailed proposal responsive to this SOW. All written deliverables shall be phrased in layperson language. Statistical and other technical terminology shall not be used without providing a glossary of terms.
The contractor shall provide uninterrupted licensing and subscription services to an electronic medical reference as stated herein.
The contractor shall provide product training, online tutorials, and promotional material. 
Contractor shall also provide unlimited support via virtual training performed by a person with a clinical background during implementation. 
Contractor shall provide technical support numbers. Customer service shall be available to provide unlimited technical support 24 hours a day, 7 days a week to troubleshoot website/connectivity issues. The contractor is expected to troubleshoot access as needed. 
The contractor shall have the ability to provide usage statistics on a quarterly basis. The format of the usage statistics is provided either via email or contractor provided login.
Contractor to provide support documentation tools, such as clinical or technical manual. 

Evaluation

Contractors shall allow a pre-identified panel of subject matter experts access to the Bayesian-guided medication dosing software to for evaluation purposes. Evaluation factors will be based on requirements and deliverables in this SOW, with focus of factors in section 5 Requirements of this SOW. A standardized list of evaluation factors will be used to evaluate requirements listed in this SOW.

Changes to Statement of Work

Any changes to this SOW shall be authorized and approved only through written correspondence from the CO. A copy of each change will be kept in a project folder along with all other products of the project. Costs incurred by the contractor through the actions of parties other than the CO shall be borne by the contractor.
Travel

The contractor is responsible for any travel expenses related to on-site training or other customer service tasks associated with deliverables.
